style_selection.method: human-selected between two real, viewed alternatives
variants_shown: A — keep Massar's visual language, port Frappe patterns only (user-model Rule 3, shipped in earlier cycles)
B — adopt Frappe CRM's actual visual system, translated to RTL/Arabic
style_selection.rationale: The founder viewed the shipped result of (A) twice and twice reported the port does not look different. He then explicitly overruled Rule 3 for visual-system scope and named (B). A human selection between two implemented, viewed alternatives is stronger evidence than designer-authored prototypes; no additional HTML variants were built, and this is recorded rather than skipped.
style_selection.rule_3_status: still governs BRANDING only — name, logo, navy sidebar, teal primary action

taste_preflight.design_read: An operations ledger, not a marketing surface: the screen's job is to fit as many campaigns on one page as Arabic legibility allows, and to spend colour only where a decision hangs on it.
taste_preflight.design_system: Frappe UI (frappe-ui token set), translated to RTL/Arabic
taste_preflight.taste_skill_scope_reason: Dashboard + data-table + record surface. TasteSkill v2 explicitly excludes these; its marketing-layout and cinematic-motion recipes are not imported. Only its foundation, a11y, and anti-slop preflight discipline applied.
checklist_notes: no em-dashes in shipped Arabic UI copy (the artifact's prose uses them; the UI does not)
a11y floor: #7C7C7C is the lightest text token (4.76:1); #999999 restricted to icons/placeholders
focus-visible specified (2px #1F7A73, offset -2px); hover carries no motion
no gradient-on-card, no glow, no shadow on list surfaces, no decorative colour

previews_note: No prototype directory: the two compared alternatives are (A) the currently deployed #kmon and (B) Frappe CRM itself, both viewed by the founder.
